papers.title: A Linear Lower Bound for Convex Body Chasing in Every Norm
papers.abstract: We establish an $\Omega(d)$ lower bound on the competitive ratio of convex body chasing in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with movement costs measured in any norm. Previously, the best known lower bound valid across all norms was $\Omega(d^{1/6})$, established by Papazov (2023); stronger lower bounds were known for $\ell_p$ norms, where Bubeck, Klartag, Lee, Li, and Sellke (2019) had established a lower bound of $\Omega(\max\{\sqrt{d}, d^{1-1/p}\})$. In particular, a linear lower bound was known only for the $\ell_\infty$ norm, realized by the standard construction of chasing faces of a hypercube. Our lower bound strictly improves on the prior universal and $\ell_p$ lower bounds for $p < \infty$ and shows that the functional Steiner point algorithm of Sellke (2023) - which has competitive ratio $O(d)$ - is asymptotically optimal for every norm. Our approach is based on the recursive construction of Bubeck, Coester, and Rabani (2023) for metrical service systems, which gives a lower bound of $\Omega(r^2)$ for requests of size $O(r)$. We show that requests in their construction, each comprising a set of discrete points in a graph metric, can be mapped to the vertices of convex requests in a $(2r+1)$-dimensional $\ell_p$ vector space while approximately preserving movement costs up to a factor of $O(r)$; the general result then follows via Milman's (1985) quotient-of-a-subspace theorem.

papers.title: New lower bounds for kissing numbers in dimensions 32-35 and 37-39
papers.abstract: We show that the kissing numbers in dimensions 32, 33, 34, 35, 37, 38 and 39 are at least 352320, 370240, 390980, 415308, 499816, 605322 and 768916, improving the previous bounds 347584, 364736, 384836, 409676, 498024, 591900 and 763668. Except in dimension 38, the configurations are those of Edel, Rains and Sloane with new binary constant-weight codes of weight 8 and minimum distance 8 in the middle layer; each additional word adds 128 points. In dimension 38 we add 6855 antipodal pairs of vectors of the second shell of the Leech lattice to the empty equator of Kravatskiy's 591612-point configuration, where 144 pairs were known; this is an independent set problem in a regular graph of degree 11178 on 8386560 vertices. The codes and lines were found by local search, and all configurations were checked pair by pair in exact integer arithmetic.

papers.title: Optimality of the $D_4$ lattice quantizer
papers.abstract: We prove that the root lattice $D_4$ uniquely minimizes the normalized second moment among four-dimensional lattices, up to similarity. The minimum is $13/(120\sqrt{2})$. The proof reduces the problem to polynomial inequalities on three secondary cones. We derive the second-moment formulas geometrically and give explicit polynomial certificates that can be checked by coefficient comparison. We also derive a lower bound for lattice quantizers in every dimension at least two from the number of Voronoi facets, using a comparison with circular cones and concavity in the solid angle. This bound strictly improves the sphere bound and recovers the hexagonal value in dimension two.

papers.title: Monge's transport problem in synthetic Lorentzian spacetimes
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of solutions to the Lorentzian Monge problem on synthetic Lorentzian spacetimes that satisfy the forward timelike measure contraction property $TMCP^+(K,N)$. The cost for this problem is the time separation function $\ell(x,y)$ (the Lorentz distance), which represents the maximum amount a particle can age when traveling from $x$ to $y$. The solution is based on the needle decomposition technique, and amounts to a reduction of the full problem to its one-dimensional counterparts. As an application of needle decomposition, we introduce the blended $TMCP$ condition, and obtain a quantitative refinement of the synthetic Hawking singularity theorem. We additionally prove a timelike nonbranching reversibility theorem for $TCD_p(K,N)$ spacetimes, showing that forward $p$-essentially nonbranching spacetimes are backward $p$-essentially nonbranching.

papers.title: Hyperrigidity and convexity in two variables
papers.abstract: We extend Brown's one-variable rigidity theorem to strictly convex functions of two variables under a regularity assumption. Let $K\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be nonempty, compact, and convex, and let $f$ be real-valued, strictly convex on $K$, and of class $C^2$ on a neighbourhood of $K$. We prove that the generating set $\{x_1,x_2,f\}$ is hyperrigid in $C(K)$.

papers.title: Quasiconformal distortion of the lower dimension and applications
papers.abstract: We study the distortion of the lower dimension and lower spectrum of sets under quasiconformal mappings. As an application, we verify weighted Hardy--Sobolev inequalities in Euclidean domains arising as quasiconformal images of domains with sufficiently regular boundaries. The regularity in question is phrased in terms of estimates for either the Assouad or the lower dimension of the complement. We also provide dilatation-dependent classification results for certain planar open sets.

papers.title: The nonexistence of nine-point crescent configurations
papers.abstract: A planar crescent configuration consists of $n$ points, no three collinear and no four concyclic, whose distinct distances have multiplicities $1,2,\ldots,n-1$. We prove by exact computation that no such configuration exists for $n=9$. The three pairs carrying the two least frequent distances yield a six-point subset with at most six distances. Rational linear algebra on quartic polynomials separates the possible six-point distance patterns into those with certified finite lists of normalized distance tuples and a residual family. Compatibility of overlapping subsets forces at least one core into the first family, without classifying the residual realizations. The remaining three points are then obtained by rational constructions over the field of the squared core distances. The multiplication matrices used to enumerate the core distances have order at most twelve. Exhaustive label assignments and exact algebraic comparisons exclude all remaining extensions.

papers.title: Balance in Inequality: Testing the Physical Equilibrium, Precession, and Structural Stability of Magic Gems
papers.abstract: A magic square exemplifies balance in inequality: its $n^2$ entries $\{1,\dots,n^2\}$ are distinct, yet every row, column, and main diagonal sums to $\mu_n=n(n^2+1)/2$. Lifting centred grid cells into $\mathbb{R}^3$ as radial vectors $\mathbf{p}_{ij}(\lambda)=(x_j,y_i,\lambda z_{ij})$ and taking their convex hull---the Magic Gem $\mathcal{G}_\lambda(S)$---asks: when does line-sum equality suffice for equilibrium in 3D, and when a nonlinear realization breaks balance, how can an opposing inequality restore it? We test this across all $880$ order-$4$ magic squares in four regimes. For radial spokes from $O$, natural lengths balance identically, while unit spokes break equilibrium on all $832$ non-associative squares in 3D and on all squares in 2D, where the ring-radius ratio $r_2/r_1=\sqrt{5}$ bounds the resultant below by the Pell convergent $9/4\approx\sqrt{5}$. By length--weight duality, balance is restored via tip weights $\mathbf{w}^*>\mathbf{0}$ on $S^2$ or power-law spoke scaling ($r^{\alpha^*}$ in 2D and $(\mathbf{V}_3)_z=0$ in 3D). In 3D rotation, equal point masses make every semi-magic square an axisymmetric top with spherical-top transition $\lambda_{\mathrm{iso}}=(n^2+1)^{-1/2}$, whereas entry masses $m_{ij}=s_{ij}$ expose the quadrupole $Q_{xy}=\sum z_{ij}x_jy_i$, triggering $180^\circ$ Dzhanibekov flips on $824$ squares. Passing to the uniform solid hull $\mathcal{G}_0(S)$ shifts the centroid off $O$ on $829$ squares; re-engaging the opposing core $\mathcal{G}_1(S)$ restores balance via two-density inclusions, nested wireframes, or the $K_{n^2}$ strut network, while all $880$ hulls unfold into non-overlapping nets with $f_0-1$ glue tabs. Finally, $\lambda=1/5$ stabilizes $74.5\%$ of facets on a table, and alternating $\mathcal{G}_\lambda(S)$ with its mirror twin $\mathcal{G}_\lambda(r^2\overline{S})=-\mathcal{G}_\lambda(S)$ locks chiral blocks into a vertical tower.

papers.title: Many Antipodal Pairs Force Many Neighboring Pairs
papers.abstract: Let $X=\{x_1,\dots,x_n\}\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a finite set of points of diameter at most $1$. It is natural to expect that if many pairs $(x_i,x_j)$ lie at distance close to $1$ from each other, then some clustering phenomenon must occur, implying that a significant number of these pairs are also very close to each other. %For $0<\varepsilon<1$, we call a pair $(x_i,x_j)$ $\varepsilon$-antipodal if $\|x_i-x_j\|\ge 1-\varepsilon$ and $\varepsilon$-neighboring if $\|x_i-x_j\|\le \varepsilon$. We prove that there exists a universal constant $c>0$ such that for all $0<\varepsilon<1$, whenever $n$ is large enough, we have: \[ \big|\{(i,j):\|x_i-x_j\|\le \varepsilon\}\big| \geq c\cdot \varepsilon^{1/2}\cdot \big|\{(i,j):\|x_i-x_j\|\geq 1-\varepsilon\}\big|. \] This confirms a recent conjecture of Steinerberger, who asked whether the $\varepsilon^{1/2}$ ratio is the best possible. We also study a two-parameter version of Steinerberger's question by considering the number of pairs at distance at most $\varepsilon_1$ and at distance at least $1-\varepsilon_2$. We show that in this case the optimal ratio is $\varepsilon_1^2\cdot\varepsilon_2^{-3/2}$ when $\varepsilon_1\leq\varepsilon_2$, and $\varepsilon_1^{1/2}$ otherwise. The proof proceeds by introducing an auxiliary graph associated with the set $X$ and reducing the problem to bounding the largest eigenvalue of its adjacency matrix. Our main result is the outcome of human--AI interactions using ChatGPT 5.4.

papers.title: Metric foundations of geometry
papers.abstract: A metric space is called all-set-homogeneous if every isometry between two of its subsets extends to an isometry of the whole space. We classify all-set-homogeneous length spaces: besides the classical examples, they include the universal metric trees of finite valence.

papers.title: An elementary proof of a tangent-cone identity for rank-one planar Lipschitz maps
papers.abstract: We give an elementary proof of a tangent-cone identity which might be known to specialists in geometric measure theory. It concerns Lipschitz mappings $g$ from the closed unit ball $B\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ to $\mathbb{R}^2$. Let $x$ be an interior point of differentiability of $g$ at which $Dg(x)$ has rank one. If the upper one-dimensional Hausdorff density of $g(B)$ at $g(x)$ is at most one, then the tangent cone to $g(B)$ at $g(x)$ coincides with the image of $Dg(x)$. This property is used in the proof of rigidity for the four-gradient problem. We provide a detailed, self-contained proof based on differentiability, connectedness and elementary estimates for one-dimensional Hausdorff measure, without using advanced methods from geometric measure theory.

papers.title: Triangulation, Volume, and Symmetries of a Dihedral Group Analogue of the Permutohedron
papers.abstract: We study an analogue of the permutohedron for the dihedral group, which we call the dihedral permutohedron. We determine the facet structure of the dihedral permutohedron, use the facet structure to construct a triangulation, and determine a nice combinatorial formula for the volume of the dihedral permutohedron. Lastly, we find a family of interesting unimodular affine symmetries of the odd dihedral permutohedron.

papers.title: Pick-up sticks problems for exponential and Pareto distributions
papers.abstract: We deal with the following two pick-up sticks problems: given an integer n greater than or equal to 3, we choose n sticks with independent random lengths from an exponential distribution or Pareto type I distribution, and we are interested in the probability that no three of them can be the sides of a triangle. In case of exponential distribution, this problem has been solved by other authors: the probability in question is equal to $n!/\big((F_3-1)(F_4-1)\cdots(F_{n+2}-1)\big)$, where $(F_i)_{i=1}^\infty$ is the sequence of Fibonacci numbers. We give a new, self-contained and detailed proof for this formula, which uses a different method compared to the earlier ones. In case of Pareto type I distribution, we derive new formulae for the corresponding probability.

papers.title: Optimal Zonotope Containment via Adaptive Gaussian Sampling
papers.abstract: We investigate the convex-body containment problem $\max\{s >0 : s Z \subseteq Q\}$, where the outer body $Q \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ is described by a membership oracle and the inner body $Z \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ is a zonotope. Our main result is a sampling-based $O(\sqrt{d/\log d})$-approximation algorithm for this problem that matches the lower bound of $\Omega(\sqrt{d/\log d})$ by Khot and Naor in the oracle model. Starting from approximate Lewis position, the algorithm samples Gaussian directions and adaptively shortens and repositions the generators. Its analysis combines preservation of the support in a fixed direction with contraction of the corresponding functional after renormalization. Crucially, the algorithm works directly with the input generators and does not use zonotope sparsification. We complement this result with a \emph{universal} $\Omega(\sqrt{d/\log d})$ lower bound holding for \emph{all} full-dimensional zonotopes when the number of oracle queries is polynomial in $d$. Finally, we consider containment problems $\max\{s >0 : s K \subseteq Q\}$, for general convex bodies $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$. A result of Nasz{\'o}di on approximating $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ by a polytope implies a $\Theta(d/\log d)$ approximation algorithm in polynomial time when the centroid of $K$ is the origin. We show the tightness of this approximation factor in the oracle model via a reduction to the circumradius computation. Our lower bound holds for centrally symmetric convex sets, implying that Barvinok's optimal $O(\sqrt{d})$-approximation of a centrally symmetric convex body by a polytope with a polynomial number of vertices cannot be computed in polynomial time.

papers.title: Attainable forms of lower spectra
papers.abstract: Let $d\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\varphi\colon(0,1)\to[0,d]$. We prove there exists a set $F\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ whose lower spectrum $\operatorname{dim}^{\theta}_{\mathrm{L}} F$ satisfies $(1-\theta)\operatorname{dim}^{\theta}_{\mathrm{L}} F = \varphi(\theta)$ for all $\theta\in(0,1)$ if and only if for all $\lambda,\theta\in(0,1)$, \begin{equation*} \varphi(\theta) \leq \varphi(\lambda\theta) - \theta \varphi(\lambda) \leq (1-\theta) d. \end{equation*} We also obtain a similar classification result for $\underline{\operatorname{dim}}^{\theta}_{\mathrm{L}} F$. In contrast to the case for Assouad spectra, it is insufficient to consider homogeneous (or uniform) sets. Instead, we follow the approach introduced by Orgov\'anyi--Rutar in arXiv:2510.07013 and proceed via a more general classification result for appropriate two-scale branching functions.

papers.title: Borelness of Moduli Spaces of Metrics Implies Separability
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a metrizable space, and let $\mathrm{Met}(X)$ denote the space of metrics compatible with the topology of $X$, regarded as a subspace of the space of continuous pseudometrics with the topology induced by the supremum metric. We first prove that if $Z$ is a discrete space whose cardinality is the first uncountable cardinal, then $\mathrm{Met}(Z)$ is not Borel. As a consequence, if $\mathrm{Met}(X)$ is Borel, then $X$ is separable. Combined with a theorem of Koshino, our result yields that the space of bounded compatible metrics on a metrizable space $X$ is completely metrizable if and only if $X$ is $\sigma$-compact. We also establish non-Archimedean analogues for spaces of ultrametrics. We further prove componentwise versions of these results, where two metrics belong to the same component if their distance is finite.

papers.title: Infinitesimal Hilbertianity for manifolds with Sobolev regular Riemannian metrics through uniform lower capacity bounds
papers.abstract: We prove that metric measure spaces arising from $2$-manifolds equipped with Riemannian metrics $g$ such that $g, g^{-1} \in L^\infty_{\rm loc} \cap W^{1,p}_{\rm loc}$ are infinitesimally Hilbertian. Along the way, we establish uniform lower $1$-capacity bounds of several $1$-dimensional subsets of $\R^2$.

papers.title: The Hibi--Li (2016) conjecture is fully resolved
papers.abstract: Hibi and Li conjectured that the order polytope $\mathcal{O}(P)$ of a finite poset $P$ has at most as many faces of each dimension as its chain polytope $\mathcal{C}(P)$, and that equality in some dimension $k$ with $1\leq k\leq|P|-1$ forces the two polytopes to be unimodularly equivalent. Fourier proved the inequality in a 2026 preprint. Let $X$ be the five-element poset in which an element lies above two incomparable elements and below two other incomparable elements. Using two results from Fourier's preprint, we show that if an $n$-element poset contains $X$ as an induced subposet, then, for every $k$ with $2\leq k\leq n-1$, its chain polytope has at least $\binom{n-3}{k-2}$ more $k$-dimensional faces than its order polytope, and that for every $n\geq5$ some $n$-element poset containing $X$ attains all these bounds at once. Since Hibi and Li showed that $\mathcal{O}(P)$ and $\mathcal{C}(P)$ are unimodularly equivalent exactly when $P$ does not contain $X$, this proves the equality statement for these values of $k$. The second version of Fourier's preprint gives an independent proof of this statement. For $k=1$, the equality statement is false: the polytopes $\mathcal{O}(X)$ and $\mathcal{C}(X)$ have the same number of edges (Hibi, Li, Sahara and Shikama) but are not unimodularly equivalent. Together with Fourier's inequality, these results settle the conjecture. The proofs given in this paper are formally verified in Lean 4.

papers.title: On higher order Morrey's inequalities over CD{\boldmath$(K,N)$}-spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish a higher order Morrey's inequality in the framework of $\mathsf{CD}(K,N)$-spaces for $K\in\mathbb{R}$ and $N\in\mathbb{N}$. We do so by first introducing an alternate version of second order Sobolev spaces in general metric measure spaces, which contains amply many functions even when $p>N$. These spaces contain the traditional $H^{2, p}(X)$ spaces on $\mathsf{RCD}(K, N)$-spaces.
